message.content:
Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. Male lions form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together—and they compete for dominance within the coalition. When a male is ready to mate, he will approach a female who is in estrus (the fertile phase of her cycle). He may display his mane, roar loudly, and perform a series of vocalizations and physical displays to attract her attention.

Once the female signals she is receptive, the male will mount her from behind and grasp her with his forepaws. The mating itself is quick, lasting only a few minutes. After copulation, the male may stay close to the female to guard her against rival males. This guarding behavior helps ensure that his sperm has the best chance of fertilizing the eggs. The entire mating season for a pride can last several weeks, during which multiple males may mate with the same female, leading to paternity confusion and increased protection for the cubs.
